description: Whether Amaterasu is the single 'supreme' deity or one of several high deities.

positions.name: Later/medieval view
positions.description: Amaterasu as the highest deity and ancestress of the emperors (the basis of state Shinto).

positions.name: Kojiki text
positions.description: The Kojiki presents her as one of the high deities sent to rule a portion of the realms, not explicitly 'above' all others.

description: The precise roles of the deities, the naming of the cave, and the role of Takemikazuchi in luring Amaterasu out.

positions.name: Kojiki version
positions.description: Ame-no-Uzume's dance, the mirror, and the assembled deities' clamor; specific naming of the cave and deities.

positions.name: Nihon Shoki version
positions.description: A related account with different wording and emphasis on the roles.

description: Whether Ōkuninushi 'yields' the land or is 'subjugated,' and the exact sequence of the Kuniyurinshi contest and the handover of the regalia.

positions.name: Kojiki version
positions.description: The sword-throw contest, the subduing of Sarutahiko, and the handover of the three regalia.

positions.name: Nihon Shoki version
positions.description: A related account with different wording of the sequence and the role of Kotohikone.

description: The details of Izanagi's descent to Yomi, the separation point, and the purification (misogi) with the birth of kami from the washed body-parts.

positions.name: Kojiki version
positions.description: The descent, the discovery of decay, the flight, the threshold-separation, and the purification with the birth of kami.

positions.name: Nihon Shoki version
positions.description: A related account with different wording of the descent and the purification.

description: Inari Ōkami's gender and the identity of the 'foxes' (messengers vs. embodiments), and the deity's precise nature.

positions.name: Female-deity view
positions.description: Inari as a female deity of rice and prosperity attended by fox messengers.

positions.name: Paired/genderless view
positions.description: Inari as a paired (male-female) or genderless deity; the foxes as embodiments rather than messengers.
